title: IdeaBlade validation metadata
description: Validation rules keyed by model type, plus an optional 'global' section. Used by both ideablade-validation (TypeScript) and IdeaBlade.Validation (.NET). See docs/metadata.md.

comment.description: A note for the people who maintain the metadata: a string, or an array of strings for one paragraph each. Ignored when validating.

global.description: Validators applied to every model type.

extends.description: Model type whose validators and properties are inherited.

condition.description: When validating an entity store, models for which this is falsy are skipped. Variables: model, entityInfos, findEntity(id, type), store(type), isClient, isServer.

validators.description: Model-level validators; they receive the whole model as value.

from.description: Inherit the rules of another model type's property: 'Customer' for the property of the same name, or 'Customer.email'. Includes the rules registered rule sources (such as Breeze's metadata) have for it.

group.description: A named group of validators. Select groups at validation time with a predicate.

validatorName.description: Name of a registered validator, e.g. 'required', 'email' or a custom validator.

async.description: Select the asynchronous validator registered under 'name'.

propertyNames.description: For a model-level validator: the properties its errors are about, such as both dates of a 'start before end' rule. Forms show the error on each of those fields.

condition.description: The validator only runs when this is truthy. Variables: model, value, context, isClient, isServer, plus registered functions.

expression.description: The 'expression' validator's expression. For 'pattern', the regular expression: a pattern string such as '^\d{5}$' (with 'flags'), or '/source/flags' such as '/^[a-z]+$/i'.

flags.description: The 'pattern' validator's regular expression flags, for a pattern given as a plain string ('/source/flags' brings its own and ignores this). 'i' (ignore case), 'm' (multiline), 's' (dotAll) and 'u' (unicode) work the same on the client and the server. Avoid 'g' and 'y': in JavaScript they make test() remember where it stopped, so a validator that runs twice can alternate between passing and failing.

expression.description: Expression in the safe expression language (a side-effect-free JavaScript subset). See docs/expressions.md.
